# Gauge

<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-component-docs.mjs from ai/component-catalog.json and ai/component-composition.json. Do not edit; run `npm run catalog:sync`. -->

`@kerfjs/ui:gauge` · Kerf UI · component · Feedback

A speedometer-style dial for a reading on a scale that is not progress, such as a live rate: a 240-degree track arc, a fill from zero to the value, and a needle scaled to max. The full variant adds ticks and the value and unit inside the dial; the bare variant is the arc, fill, and needle alone at chip height, as a named meter.

## When to use

Show a live rate or level against a ceiling at a glance (tokens per minute, tickets updated per hour) on a stats tile, a chip, or a standby display.

- A live rate or level on a glance surface: pass value, max, a label, and optional valueText and unit.
- A chip-height indicator beside other status: variant="bare", which carries the value in its accessible name and hover title.
- A themed display such as a night palette: pass colors with typed CssColor values instead of writing CSS.

**Not when:**

- Do not use it for progress toward done; use ProgressBar or ProgressRing.
- Do not use it where a precise number matters more than the glance; show the number in Text.
- Do not target its classes to recolor it; pass tone or colors.

**Alternatives:**

- [ProgressRing](./progress-ring.md) (nearest) — Use a ProgressRing for compact progress toward done.
- [ProgressBar](./progress-bar.md) (nearest) — Use a ProgressBar for measurable progress with a label row.

## Imports

- JavaScript: `@kerfjs/ui/gauge` — exports `Gauge`, `GaugeProps`, `GaugeVariant`, `GaugeColors`, `GaugeRootAttributes`, `ProgressTone`.
- CSS: the browser build of `@kerfjs/ui/gauge` pulls its CSS automatically; import `@kerfjs/ui/gauge.css` manually only without the `browser` export condition.
- Declared side effects: browser-condition-css.

## Props

Exact prop names and types: [`@kerfjs/ui/gauge`](../public-api-signatures-v1.md#kerfjsuigauge) in `public-api-signatures-v1.md`. Do not infer props from examples.

**Variants (configure, do not restyle):**

- full (ticks, value, and unit)
- bare (arc, fill, and needle)
- brand, success, warning, or danger tone
- pinned at the end when the value exceeds max

## Composition

- Parents: any.
- Contexts: `application-ui`.
- Children: unrestricted.

## State and wiring

**The app owns:** the value, max, valueText, and unit; the label; the variant, tone, size, and any colors.

No wiring helper.

## Geometry

Margin: none · border: none · padding: none (layout role: feedback). `self` means the component already owns it — do not add wrapper padding, margin, or borders around it.

- Its width is size (88px full, 40px bare by default) and its height follows the dial; the drawing scales with the width.

## Accessibility

- It is role meter named by label, with aria-valuemin 0, aria-valuemax max, aria-valuenow clamped to max, and aria-valuetext set to the value text and unit; the SVG is decorative.
- A bare gauge also sets a hover title of the label and value.
- The needle and fill transition only when the value changes and hold still under prefers-reduced-motion or the static-effects switch; forced colors draw a GrayText track, a Highlight fill, and a CanvasText needle and readout.

## Styling boundary

The component owns its own styles. Configure it through its props and variants; do not override its internals.

Public class hooks (select for layout placement only, never to change the component's look): `kui-gauge`, `kui-gauge__track`, `kui-gauge__fill`, `kui-gauge__tick`, `kui-gauge__tick--major`, `kui-gauge__needle`, `kui-gauge__value`, `kui-gauge__unit`.

Never put `kui-gauge`, `kui-gauge__track`, `kui-gauge__fill`, `kui-gauge__tick`, `kui-gauge__tick--major`, `kui-gauge__needle`, `kui-gauge__value`, `kui-gauge__unit` on an element you write; render `Gauge` instead (`KUI-L103`).

Everything else is internal: `kerf-ui-analyze` reports private or unknown `.kui-*` selectors (`KUI-L001`, `KUI-L010`), unknown or private tokens (`KUI-L002`, `KUI-L012`), and any application rule that restyles the component, forced dimensions included (`KUI-L019`).
